name: Mancala Meridian
description: A direct revival of the ancient mancala family of games, played on hand-carved wooden or salvaged-plastic boards with scavenged stones, beads, or synth-protein pellets as seeds — the original rules unchanged since antiquity. The game spread through GLMZ's Shelf communities via West African, North African, and Southeast Asian diaspora networks, reclaimed as an explicitly analog, zero-tech social ritual. No corporate version exists; the game is taught person-to-person, boards are made by hand, and rules vary by community tradition.
story_hooks: A mancala board carved in 2186 by a community elder has been passed down through three families and contains notches that, read as a code, map a network of pre-corponation underground tunnels beneath the Shelf.
The community tournament has been infiltrated by a Tier 3 academic documenting 'pre-collapse game culture' whose recording equipment is also harvesting biometric data on all players — for whom?
Two rival Shelf factions have agreed to settle a resource dispute through a best-of-seven mancala series rather than violence, and a PC has been asked to referee — and to ensure neither side cheats.
